Media Opps: Floodlight, NBCUniversal, Los Angeles Times
Write about the plastics industry for $2 per word
November 13, 2026
Media Opps: Floodlight, NBCUniversal, Los Angeles Times
Write about the plastics industry for $2 per word
STUDY HALL COURSES:
▶ Pitch Workshop: Master the Art of Storytelling
In this live Study Hall
course
, Adam Popescu — a narrative journalist and author whose work has appeared in The New York Times, Bloomberg, and many other outlets — will cover everything from identifying stories to securing assignments. This workshop will focus on pitching (so bring your pitches!) and cover what it takes to succeed in the competitive world of freelance journalism using practical tips and techniques that have helped him build a career at some of the world's most prestigious publications. There will also be a Q&A with Adam at the end of the course.
The 1.5-hour
course
will take place
Monday, November 16th, at 10 AM / 1 PM ET
. The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “studyhallmember” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email
support@studyhall.xyz
.
Interview with Eve Sneider
On the latest Study Hall Podcast
episode
, Eve Sneider discussed her new book
The Absent Woman: The Genius of Janet Malcolm
. Sneider talked about how Janet Malcolm’s writing foreshadowed Nathan Fielder’s
You Can See Everything
, and what contemporary writers can learn from Malcolm’s deconstructive approach to reporting.
Listen
here
.
How Janet Malcolm Foreshadowed "You Can See Everything" ft. Eve Sneider
Podcast Episode · The Study Hall Podcast · November 9 · 35m
Apple Podcasts
The listings are now posted throughout the week on our
Opportunity Finder
.
If you have any technical questions or want to submit an opportunity m, please email ‘
support AT studyhall DOT xyz
with “Opps:” in the subject line.
Please note:
Anything marked as “
NEW
” is from the past seven days and is included alongside newly added opps (but more than one week old). Finally, old opps from previous issues with upcoming deadlines are listed at the end of the newsletter.
OTHER RESOURCES
▶ Add to the Rate-Sharing Database
The
Freelance Solidarity Project
maintains an ongoing
Rate Sharing Database
to build a clearer picture of freelance pay—and, ultimately, change how we are paid. Add your rates, and help build a more equitable future for freelancers in the industry.
The latest party in the Deez Drinks event series is
"The Publishing Party,"
bringing together everyone in New York's publishing industry and book biz together under one roof for a night (and with an open bar) on Oct. 27. All literary-minded folks are welcome,
tickets
are $20.
Writers Sarah Miller and A.S. Hamrah are teaching a two-day (in person and on Zoom from November 14 and 15t)
writing class
about using “humor as a weapon.” The class will show you how to “get comfortable with strong feelings and opinions required for memorable writing” and “understand how to make things you think are funny funny to others.” More info
here
.
The Institute for Independent Journalists have opened registration for the
Fall 2026 Business of Freelancing course
, offered from Oct. 1 through Nov. 19.
This eight-week, live online course provides a comprehensive foundation in the business of freelance journalism and has sold out every time they’ve presented it. Each session combines real-world strategy with personalized guidance, covering topics such as rate setting, time and income management, client relationships, and long-term planning.
Registration is $299.
They’ve also announced
their lineup of webinars
for freelancers, featuring assigning editors, fellowship directors, and independent creators. Each webinar runs from 12-1:15 pm EST and costs $30.
Nov. 20 Fund your Freelancing with Fellowships and Grants
Dec. 11 Pitching Arts, Culture, and Travel Stories
Jan. 22 Winning Revenue Strategies for Creator Journalists
Feb. 4-5 Pitch the Editors: Sign Up for 1:1 Pitch Sessions
CALLS FOR PITCHES
Please note:
We are not endorsing every publication or company listed here. Engaging with a publication or company is entirely up to the reader. We currently sort each section from the most to least recently posted.
Final note:
Before pitching,
always
check the links to confirm the opportunities are still available.
TIME-SENSITIVE PITCH CALLS
NEW:
-Floodlight is
calling for pitches
for 1,000 to 2,000-word investigations into the plastics industry. Contributors will pursue clear accountability angles examining plastic pollution, public health effects, industry lobbying, disinformation, and greenwashing, with priority given to stories highlighting environmental injustices affecting vulnerable communities. The publication is seeking freelance journalists with relevant writing samples to deliver thoroughly fact-checked stories
slated for January publication
. Pay is $2 per word. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Nov 25)
EVERGREEN PITCH CALLS
NEW:
-The Sick Times is
calling for pitches
for reported news features and commentary essays covering Long COVID and related chronic diseases. Contributors will examine scientifically backed treatment options, related conditions such as ME and dysautonomia, disability justice, international reporting, public records investigations, service journalism, and novel perspectives tailored to chronically ill readers and allies. The publication prioritizes proposals from writers with Long COVID and related conditions and is seeking original, human-written pitches—not full drafts—that make complex topics accessible to a general audience. Pay is $1,300 for reported news features of 1,500 to 1,700 words and $400 for essays of 1,000 to 1,200 words. Pitch by emailing
editors@thesicktimes.org
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.

Contributors will examine emerging research and complex questions across psychology and related disciplines such as philosophy, history, and anthropology to help readers better understand themselves and navigate everyday life. The publication is seeking proposals from psychologists, researchers, academics, and working journalists capable of delivering original, human-written reported essays or expert analyses. Pay is about $750 for academics and professionals and $2,000 for working journalists writing reported essays. Pitch by emailing
pamela.weintraub@aeon.co

Opps Finder listing

Candidates should have three to five years of professional experience as a reporter covering a local beat, and be an independent journalist or employed at a newsroom willing to provide a year-long sabbatical. Submissions may include single stories, series of up to four related pieces, audio features or podcasts up to 30 minutes, or video broadcasts under 10 minutes that demonstrate deep narrative storytelling. Prizes are $5,000 for first place and $2,500 for second place in the professional category, and $2,500 for the student winner.
